name: co-walker

attributes.attribute: seen near the moment of death
may be a fairy in disguise

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A co-walker is a figure in the folklore of Ireland and Scotland. At the time of a death, a double of the dead one was seen walking about. A dying woman might appear in church, or a dead man at his own wake. Some spoke of these pairs as twin souls freed by death. Others said they were fairies in the shape of the dead. One test was never to speak to these shadows, who would soon depart.

okr.objective: A co-walker is the double of a dead person seen at the hour of death.
key_results: A double of the dead one is seen at the time of death.
Some call the pair twin souls set free.
Others say the shade is a fairy in disguise.
People were told never to speak to the co-walker.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
